subject.title: feat(onboarding): offer detected Claude Code/Codex/Hermes memory imports across CLI, macOS, and Linux onboarding

question: Should memory import become a standard detection-gated step in every local first-run onboarding flow, or remain an explicit post-onboarding migration/settings action?
rationale: This changes first-run UX across four surfaces and writes persistent memory into the workspace; the protected maintainer label requires explicit ownership of that product direction rather than inferring approval from implementation quality.

options.title: Sponsor after hardening
options.body: Approve the cross-platform onboarding direction once the apply hang is fixed and complete Linux/macOS first-run proof is attached.

options.title: Keep import explicit
options.body: Retain the existing CLI migration and Control UI Settings entry points without adding an automatic first-run offer.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after hardening
recommendation.body: Approve the cross-platform onboarding direction once the apply hang is fixed and complete Linux/macOS first-run proof is attached.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available current-history routing candidate for the shipped Claude migration and onboarding surfaces.
